newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says 96 budget deficit under 200 mln dinars.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says 96 budget deficit under 200 mln dinars.

text.p: Finance Minister Marwan Awad said on Tuesday Jordan's 1996 budget deficit would not exceed 200 million dinars ($282 million), the official news agency Petra reported.
Awad's estimate indicated the deficit could be substantially higher than the official 163 million dinar the government forecast when the budget was presented at the start of the year.
But it was lower than some economists had feared after record world wheat prices sent Jordan's import bill soaring in the first half of 1996.

Awad, briefing members of the finance committee of the lower house of parliament on government economic policy, did not say whether the forecast deficit in the 1.8 billion dinar 1996 budget had factored in foreign assistance.
Jordan's 1995 budget deficit, before foreign grants, stood at around 114 million dinars. Grants and loans have traditionally covered budget deficit shortfalls.
The government hoped the deficit would be cut from a forecast 4.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in the 1996 budget to 3.1 percent of GDP in the 1997 budget, Awad said.
Economists say next year's budget will not be substantially higher than the 1996 budget.

Jordan initially forecast a bigger 1996 budget deficit because of the rising world wheat prices, which prompted the government in August to end subsidies on bread -- sparking Jordan's worst riots since 1989.
The steep bread price rise and lower world grain prices since then have helped to considerably reduce the budget deficit, economists say.

Awad also said the government was engaged in debt-equity swap talks with Jordan's major Western creditor nations to transfer into direct investment some of Jordan's foreign debt of more than $6 billion.
